headline: Chips claw back part of Thursday's rout (SOX +4.2%) as a hot jobs report lifts hike bets
summary: Nasdaq futures bounced before the open and the index was up nearly 2% at its high, but the gains faded through the afternoon as yields firmed after the strong payrolls data, leaving the S&P 500 up 0.3%. The rebound was concentrated in semiconductors and tech, with technology and communication services leading the sector table, while the Dow slipped as Apple and Microsoft lagged. Small caps joined in, the Russell 2000 rising 0.9%, and the VIX eased back from Thursday's spike.
drivers: After the SOX's 12% plunge on fears of curbs on new US data centers, buyers stepped back into the hardest-hit names: AMD jumped 11%, Lam Research about 8%, Intel nearly 8%, Qualcomm and Marvell over 5%, Micron about 5% and Nvidia 2.8%. Chip stocks alone added roughly half a point to the S&P 500, but the SOX recovered only about a third of Thursday's loss.
Blowout payrolls revive December hike bets

The US added 165,000 jobs in October against about 65,000 expected, unemployment dipped to 4.1% and wages rose 0.4% on the month, with prior months revised up by 84,000. Futures priced about a 77% chance of a December Fed hike, the 2-year yield rose about 5bp to roughly 4.52% and the curve flattened, which capped the rally in the afternoon.
Dow lags as megacaps and rate-sensitive names slip
Apple and Microsoft slipped, keeping the Dow down 237 points, while higher yields weighed on rate-sensitive sectors and energy and banks were flat to lower.

JFrog soared about 35% and IonQ about 23% on raised guidance, while DraftKings sank about 21% on a wider-than-expected loss, Axon fell 18% after cutting its 2026 revenue outlook and Atlassian dropped about 16% on a weak data-center revenue guide.
week: For the week the S&P 500 fell 2.7%, the Nasdaq 3.4% (its fourth straight weekly loss), the Russell 2000 2.1% and the Dow 0.9%, the S&P's worst week since spring 2025; WTI crude lost about 12.8% on hopes of de-escalation in the Iran war, and the Fed is now seen as likely to hike again in December.
watch: Next: October CPI next week is the main test for December Fed pricing, and any further word on state or federal limits to data-center construction will steer the chip and AI names.
